results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Rising Waters.
results.text:
I built a mono-blue Rising Waters deck that locks the opponent's lands. It's a brew: no published Premodern list in the last 400 days runs Rising Waters, so the base comes from the Merfolk deck, which wins the same way with Winter Orb.

**The plan:** Rising Waters means lands don't untap normally, and each player untaps only one land per upkeep. You play cheap creatures on turns 1–2, then cast Rising Waters, ideally on turn 3 using Sea Scryer's mana. After that the opponent can use about one mana a turn while you keep attacking. Your Lords of Atlantis give your other Merfolk islandwalk, and Cloud of Faeries and Gilded Drake fly. You barely need mana under the lock. Daze, Gush and Foil can all be cast without paying mana. Daze and Gush also return tapped Islands to your hand, and you replay one untapped as your land drop. Sea Scryer is a creature that makes mana, so the lock doesn't stop it. Cloud of Faeries untaps two lands when it enters, so it costs you nothing to cast.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-blue Merfolk with the free-counterspell package (chosen).** It takes the Daze / Gush / Foil / Counterspell set from Stiflenought on your list, and Merfolk shows that cheap creatures plus Winter Orb already works.
2. **Blue-green mana creatures with Opposition,** borrowed from Cradle Control. Creatures that make mana untap normally under the lock.
3. **A Bant deck with Armageddon and Mox Diamond,** borrowed from Terrageddon.

I chose the first because the cards you cast without mana and the Islands you return and replay are the only package that gets stronger under your own lock, not just tolerates it.

**Honest odds:**
- You'll have Rising Waters by turn 4 about 53% of the time.
- The two Winter Orbs, which are a cheaper version of the same lock, raise that to 68% for any lock piece.
- The full turn-by-turn sequence I listed for the submission (Rootwater Mystic, Sea Scryer, Rising Waters, Lord, Daze, Gush) comes together only about 3% of the time. That's because it needs six specific cards. In practice the deck wins with any mix of cheap creatures, a lock piece and a free counterspell.

**Other notes:**
- I cut Unsummon for 1 Chain of Vapor, after the deck checker pointed out that players almost always choose Chain of Vapor for that slot. It also bounces enchantments and artifacts, like Opalescence or Parallax Wave.
- The deck runs 18 lands, the same as real Merfolk lists. The two Wastelands are much stronger when the opponent is stuck on one untapped land.
- The sideboard is aimed at the decks on your list. It has Annul for Enchantress, Hydroblast and Chill against Sligh and Goblins, Tormod's Crypt for Hermit Druid, and Submerge, which is free against green decks.

--- After playtest ---
I made all three fixes, one of them a little differently from the suggestion. The revised deck passed the legality check and was accepted.

1. **Foil → 3 Mana Leak (fixed as suggested).** Foil needed an Island card in hand, and the deck rarely had one to spare. Mana Leak costs {1}{U} and counters unless the caster pays {3}. Under Rising Waters, where each player untaps only one land per upkeep, the opponent almost never has 3 mana left over. So it works like a hard counter and fits the lock better than Foil did.
2. **Mana: cut both Wastelands for 2 Islands (instead of a Wasteland and a Polluted Delta).** The Wastelands were the only lands that couldn't make blue. Polluted Delta fetches an Island, so it already counts as a blue source. Now all 18 lands make blue: 12 Island, 4 Flooded Strand, 2 Polluted Delta. The extra Islands also help Daze and Gush. One correction: the deck has 18 lands, not 22 as the review said.
3. **Gilded Drake → 2 more Chain of Vapor, for 3 total (fixed as suggested).** Drake only swaps for a creature, and that's too narrow. Chain of Vapor costs {U} and bounces any nonland permanent, so it can move a blocker or a problem enchantment or artifact. If the opponent wants to copy it, they have to sacrifice a land, which they can't afford while Rising Waters is out. This is part of the deck's own tempo plan, not a card just for the Enchantress matchup.

The plan is the same: early Merfolk and Sea Scryer, Rising Waters on turn 3, then protect the lock with counters while islandwalking Lords win the game.

The tool reported that you'll have drawn every card in the win line by turn 7 in only 0.4% of games. That number is low mainly because the line names eight specific cards, and the tool doesn't count the card draw from Gush. You don't need every one of them to win, but it's a real measure of how often the full line comes together.

playtest.game:
Keep: 2 lands, Foil, Counterspell, 2 Lords and Drake. It's risky but has interaction against a slow deck (in hindsight, a mulligan). On the play.
T1: Island. Opp: Forest, Utopia Sprawl.
T2: draw Counterspell, play Wasteland (U + C). Opp casts Argothian Enchantress. Foil is uncastable because I have no Island card in hand to discard, and Counterspell needs UU. It resolves. Drake has no legal target (shroud).
T3: draw Lord, no land. UU Lords are stuck on one blue source. Opp: Enchantress's Presence plus Wild Growth, drawing 2-3 cards per turn.
T4: draw Gush, no land. Gush needs 2 Islands on the battlefield. Opp: Mirri's Guile, Seal of Cleansing, Serra's Sanctum. I Wasteland the Sanctum at end of turn (left with 1 Island).
T5: draw Island, play it, cast Lord of Atlantis. Opp: Elephant Grass, so each attacker costs 2. Islandwalk is irrelevant against Forests.
T6: draw Island, play it (3 Islands), hold Counterspell. Opp casts Solitary Confinement; I Counterspell it. They follow with a second Sanctum and Sterling Grove.
T7: draw Island (4 Islands). Cast the second Lord with UU and keep 2 up; Foil is still dead (I discard Island + card later). Lords are 2/2s that can't profitably attack through Grass.
T8: draw Daze. Gush, returning 2 Islands, draws Daze plus a blank. Opp fights through my Daze and Foil with spare mana and resolves Replenish/Opalescence. That gives a board of large enchantment creatures plus a recurring Confinement.
T9: My board is 2 Lords, opponent at 20 life. They are locked under Confinement plus Sanctum mana, and I have no answer to resolved enchantments. Rising Waters and Winter Orb were never drawn; Orb would barely matter against Wild Growth and Sprawl anyway. Loss.

problems.problem: Foil was dead for most of the game. It needs an Island card in hand, but the deck runs only 10 basics, uses 6 fetches that can't be discarded, and Gush and Daze also want Islands. A 'free' counter that is rarely free is an expensive 4-mana card in a mana-starved Rising Waters deck.
problems.fix: Cut 3 Foil for 3 Mana Leak: a cheap hard-ish counter that fits a lock deck short on mana.

problems.problem: The mana can't support the UU costs. Lord of Atlantis, Counterspell and Patron Wizard (UUU) all want multiple blue, but 2 of the 22 lands are colorless Wastelands. The opening hand sat on one blue source with two Lords and Counterspell uncastable for four turns.
problems.fix: Cut 1 Wasteland and 1 Polluted Delta for 2 Island. More basics also power Daze, Gush and Foil-style alternate costs.

problems.problem: Gilded Drake is a narrow creature-swap that did nothing against a deck with few creatures and a shroud engine (Argothian Enchantress). The deck has only one Chain of Vapor to answer a resolved enchantment, artifact or lock piece, and every permanent the opponent resolved stuck.
problems.fix: Cut 2 Gilded Drake for 2 more Chain of Vapor: flexible bounce for any nonland permanent that is also cheap tempo under Rising Waters.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Mind Over Matter.
results.text:
I built a **blue-black Mind Over Matter / Kamahl reanimator brew** for Premodern. It's legal and was accepted.

**How it wins:** Mind Over Matter (MoM) lets you discard a card to untap a creature. Kamahl, Pit Fighter has haste and taps to deal 3 damage to any target. With both on the battlefield, every card in your hand becomes another 3 damage: seven taps is 21. You never pay for either 6-drop:
- **Kamahl:** discard him with Careful Study, Frantic Search or Buried Alive, then bring him back with Reanimate, Animate Dead or Shallow Grave.
- **MoM:** put it into play with Show and Tell, or hardcast it using Ancient Tomb and Lotus Petal.
- **Arcanis:** the backup engine. Each discard untaps him, and each tap draws 3, so you gain 2 cards a loop and keep the Kamahl damage going.

Once MoM is out, it can discard Kamahl into the graveyard itself, so MoM + Kamahl in hand + a reanimation spell is a full kill.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Blue-white Replenish:** borrow the Attunement / Frantic Search / Intuition / Replenish package from the field list to discard MoM and bring it back. It has no real kill, because MoM has nothing worth untapping there.
2. **Mono-blue Dream Halls / Show and Tell:** cheat MoM in and finish with Arcanis. It's slow, since Arcanis can't tap the turn it arrives.
3. **Blue-black reanimator with Kamahl (my pick):** the only real Premodern list with MoM is a four-color Rogue deck built on Kamahl and Arcanis. I kept that engine, plus Frantic Search and Intuition from the Replenish package, and added the Reanimator deck's shell (Reanimate, Animate Dead, Careful Study, Lotus Petal). Show and Tell replaces that list's Academy Rector trick for getting MoM out.

I picked it because it's the only direction where MoM turns your hand straight into damage, and Kamahl brought back on turn 2 is a real threat even without MoM.

**Odds and caveats:**
- **Assembly odds:** you'll naturally have a way to get MoM, a reanimation spell and a way to get Kamahl into the graveyard about 45% of the time by turn 4. By turn 5 it's about 80% when Careful Study, Frantic Search and Intuition count as digging for him (draw-odds tool, no mulligans). The submit tool's 0.2% figure means drawing every card named in the line, Arcanis included, with no tutors counted; it isn't the real chance to assemble the combo.
- **Kamahl is fragile:** he has 1 toughness, so Sligh and Goblins can kill him easily. Shallow Grave at instant speed, ideally at the end of the opponent's turn, helps you go off before they can answer him.
- **"No red sources" warning:** the checker flags that Kamahl is red. That's on purpose; you never cast him.
- **Land count:** 18 lands is more than real Reanimator lists run (about 14). That's on purpose too, because you sometimes need to hardcast MoM.

The sideboard is aimed at the decks the meta tool shows: Hydroblast, Smother, Diabolic Edict, Engineered Plague, Defense Grid and Tormod's Crypt.

--- After playtest ---
The revised deck was accepted. I took one suggested fix as given, changed one, and turned one down.

1. **Frantic Search stays.** The legality lookup lists it as legal in Premodern, not banned. It shows up in 134 recent lists, mostly Replenish decks. It's free card selection that puts Kamahl in the graveyard, so cutting it would only weaken the deck.
2. **Mana: −1 Swamp, +1 Island instead of −2/+2.** Polluted Delta can only fetch a basic Island or Swamp, and Underground River isn't a basic. With no Swamps at all, Delta could never make black, and Reanimate, Animate Dead, Duress and Buried Alive need it. Keeping one Swamp gives about 13 black sources while blue rises to 19. Show and Tell is still the main way to get Mind Over Matter out. Hardcasting it with Ancient Tomb and Lotus Petal is the backup.
3. **−3 Shallow Grave, +3 Counterspell.** Shallow Grave was the weakest reanimation spell: it returns only the top creature, and that creature is exiled at end of turn. Counterspell isn't only for this matchup. Mind Over Matter decks can't remove an enchantment once it's in play, so stopping Solitary Confinement, Worship or Seal of Cleansing before they resolve is the only defence. It also protects Show and Tell. That still leaves 7 reanimation spells (4 Reanimate, 3 Animate Dead).

The win line hasn't changed. Get Kamahl into the graveyard, reanimate him, Show and Tell in Mind Over Matter, then discard cards to untap Kamahl for 3 damage each. The target is turn 4.

**Odds:** the submission check put the chance of naturally drawing every card in the line by turn 4 at 0.2%. That figure ignores Intuition, Buried Alive and the card-draw spells, so the real chance is higher. This is still a fragile combo deck, not a consistent one.

The checker also warned that the deck has only 4 red sources for Kamahl. You never pay his cost, because he only enters through reanimation or Show and Tell, so you can ignore it.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Phyrexian Processor.
results.text:
I built and submitted a mono-black deck that uses Dark Ritual and fast lands to cast Phyrexian Processor on turn 1 or 2. It's a brew, not a proven list. Processor hardly shows up in recent results. The only recent appearances are 4 lists in 90 days, mostly in Devourer Combo sideboards, so there was no Processor deck to copy.

**The plan:** Cast Processor early with Dark Ritual, Mox Diamond, Ancient Tomb or City of Traitors. When it enters, pay about 6 life, or less against burn decks. From the next turn on, spend 4 mana to make a 6/6 every turn. The fastest version is turn 1: Swamp, Dark Ritual and Mox Diamond make 4 mana. The usual version is turn 2, which takes two lands plus either Ritual, Ancient Tomb or Mox. Duress, Cabal Therapy and Ravenous Rats take away the cards that answer Processor or its tokens, like counterspells and Swords to Plowshares. Smother, Diabolic Edict and Masticore deal with creatures. Phyrexian Negator and Hypnotic Specter are early threats that the fast mana makes even stronger.

**Honest odds:** With 4 copies and no legal tutor in mono-black (Vampiric Tutor is banned and Demonic Tutor isn't legal), you'll see Processor by turn 3 in about 49% of games. In the other games you're playing a Ritual deck with Negator and Specter, which is still a real deck. The checker reports 2.8% for drawing every card in my exact turn-5 sequence, but that sequence is just one example and the deck doesn't need it.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Ritual-Processor on the Moneyball Black shell (chosen):** Moneyball's discard and removal, plus Ancient Tomb and City of Traitors borrowed from Welder Prison.
2. **Colorless prison in the Welder Prison style:** Tinker, Tangle Wire and Thran Dynamo, with Processor as the win condition.
3. **Mono-red Sol lands:** Ancient Tomb and City of Traitors with Tangle Wire and burn.

I picked the first because Dark Ritual is the only cheap way in Premodern to reliably cast Processor on turn 1 or 2. Also, black's discard is the best way to protect an expensive artifact you've already paid life for. In the prison version, Processor would be one card among many lock pieces rather than the focus.

**Sideboard:**
- Dystopia and Gloom against Enchantress and white decks
- Engineered Plague against Goblins and other creature decks
- Tormod's Crypt against Hermit Druid and Replenish
- Bottle Gnomes and the third Masticore against Sligh
- Snuff Out against Dreadnought and other non-black threats

--- After playtest ---
I made all three fixes, but the first one had to change: Hymn to Tourach is banned in Premodern, so I used Funeral Charm instead. The revised deck is accepted, is legal and is still exactly 60 cards.

1. **Removal that did nothing against Enchantress:** I cut 2 Diabolic Edict for 2 Funeral Charm.
   - It costs one black mana and can be cast at instant speed. It makes the opponent discard a card, which works against Enchantress and control decks.
   - Its +2/-1 mode kills creatures with 1 toughness, so it still helps against Goblins and Elves.
   - I kept 3 Smother in the main deck for creature decks. Against Enchantress, board Smother out for more discard.

2. **Colorless lands fighting the black costs:** I cut 2 City of Traitors for 2 Swamp, as suggested. That gives 16 Swamps plus Mox Diamond, so Hypnotic Specter and turn-1 Duress or Cabal Therapy get cast on time. Fast Processor starts still come from Ancient Tomb, Dark Ritual and Mox Diamond.

3. **Processor cast with no protection:** I cut 1 Masticore for 1 Unmask, as suggested. The deck now has 12 discard effects: 4 Duress, 3 Cabal Therapy, 1 Unmask, 2 Funeral Charm and 2 Ravenous Rats. The plan is to strip Seal of Cleansing, Disenchant or Solitary Confinement first, then cast Processor. I added only one Unmask because casting it for free means exiling a black card from your hand, which costs you a card. The cut Masticore stays in the sideboard next to the existing one.

**How often the full win line comes together:** The deck checker estimates you'll have drawn every card in the win line by turn 5 in only about 3% of games. That number doesn't count other cards that fill the same roles, like Mind Stone or other discard, so the deck works more often than that. Even so, expect a turn-2 Processor to be rare.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Volrath's Shapeshifter and Phage the Untouchable.
results.text:
I built a BUG Survival deck called "Untouchable Shapeshifter." Volrath's Shapeshifter copies the full text of whatever creature card is on top of your graveyard. So the deck never casts Phage. It puts Phage on top of the graveyard at the right moment, and Shapeshifter becomes a Phage that deals combat damage to the opponent, which makes them lose the game.

**How it wins**
1. **Turn 2:** with a mana creature out, cast Survival of the Fittest. Its ability ({G}, discard a creature card: search for a creature) works at instant speed. It's an ability, not a spell, so no spell card lands on top of the discarded creature.
2. **Turn 3:** cast Shapeshifter. Use Survival to put Dauthi Horror on top of the graveyard and fetch Phage. Shapeshifter now has shadow (it can only be blocked by other shadow creatures).
3. **Turn 4:** attack. Once no blockers are declared, discard Phage, either with Shapeshifter's own "{2}: Discard a card" or as Survival's cost. Blocks are already locked in, so Shapeshifter stays unblocked even though it loses shadow. It deals damage as Phage, and the opponent loses.
- Phage's drawback ("if you didn't cast it from your hand, you lose the game") never applies. Phage never enters the battlefield; Shapeshifter is already there and just takes on its text.
- Shapeshifter's discard ability is always on its card, so you can also just hold Phage in hand.

**Directions I considered**
- **UB Psychatog shell** (Counterspell, Duress, Gush from the menu): it protects the combo well but has no way to search for Phage or Shapeshifter.
- **Hermit Druid Combo shell:** this is where Shapeshifter actually shows up in results (81 of 90 lists). But Hermit Druid buries your library in random order, so you can't pick which creature ends up on top.
- **BUG Survival (chosen):** Survival both searches for every piece and acts as a free instant-speed discard outlet, so it turns two awkward cards into a two-card kill.

**The rest of the deck**
- The engine draws on BG Survival: Birds of Paradise, Wall of Roots, Llanowar Elves, Wall of Blossoms and Survival targets like Bone Shredder, Mesmeric Fiend, Ravenous Baloth and Uktabi Orangutan.
- Duress, Cabal Therapy and Smother protect the combo.
- The deck runs 20 lands, close to BG Survival's average of 20.6. The checker compared it to Hermit Druid Combo, which runs 22 lands with no basics across five colors, so those land numbers don't really apply here.

**Honest odds**
- You'll see Shapeshifter, Survival or Worldly Tutor by turn 4 about 86% of the time on the play.
- The checker found that all four combo cards are naturally in hand by turn 4 only about 2% of the time. That number ignores tutors, and Survival or Worldly Tutor can find every piece, so the real turn-4 rate depends mostly on drawing Survival plus a mana creature.
- Turns 5 and 6 are the more realistic kill turns.
- **Weak spots:** instant-speed removal on Shapeshifter in response to the discard, and opposing shadow creatures (rare in this field).

The sideboard has Naturalize, Pernicious Deed, Engineered Plague, Hydroblast, Tormod's Crypt and Xantid Swarm for the top decks in the meta.

--- After playtest ---
I made all three suggested fixes, with one small change to the third. The new list passed the deck check and was accepted.

1. **No answers to enchantments:** I cut Uktabi Orangutan for Elvish Lyrist. It costs {G}, and you can pay {G}, tap it and sacrifice it to destroy target enchantment. results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Seismic Assault.
results.text:
I built a red-green "Seismic Lands" deck. It's a brew that borrows Terrageddon's lands-in-the-graveyard package. The plan: get Mox Diamond into play on turn 1 by discarding a land, which helps you cast Seismic Assault (RRR) on turn 2 or 3. From then on every spare land in hand is a 2-damage shot at a creature or the opponent's face. Every land you throw also grows Terravore, and so do cracked Wooded Foothills, used Wastelands and the Mox discard. Groundskeeper pays {1}{G} to return a basic land from your graveyard, so spare mana turns into repeated burn. You win by turn 5 to 6 with a huge trampling Terravore plus Seismic shots, and Lightning Bolt and Fire // Ice finish the last points of damage.

**The three directions I sketched:**
- **Mono-red, 28 lands:** Seismic as card advantage in a burn deck.
- **Blue-red Dream Halls:** the only real Premodern list running Seismic Assault, but there it's a side card, not the plan.
- **Red-green, borrowing Terrageddon's package (my pick):** Mox Diamond, Terravore, Sylvan Library and Wasteland. I chose it because Seismic's cost (discarding lands) is exactly what that package feeds on. Every shot is also a power and toughness boost for Terravore, so the enchantment becomes a two-part win condition rather than just a burn engine.

**Things to know:**
- **Finding Seismic:** with 4 copies plus 2 Gamble, you have one by turn 3 in about 64% of games (on the play, no mulligans).
- **Why only 2 Gamble:** its random discard can throw away the card you just found.
- **Lands:** 25, which is a lot. That's on purpose, because spare lands are ammunition.
- **Fire // Ice:** treat it as just Fire. Only Gemstone Mine and Mox Diamond can make blue mana for Ice.
- **The win-line odds look scary but aren't:** the checker gives 0.6% to have drawn *every* card in my win line by turn 5. That's because the line lists six specific cards. The deck only actually needs Seismic or Terravore plus lands.
- **Sideboard:** aimed at the current field. Pyroclasm is for Goblins, Sligh and Hermit Druid. Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast are for Stiflenought and Psychatog. Naturalize and Anarchy are for Enchantress. Tormod's Crypt is for Hermit Druid and Psychatog. Zuran Orb is for Sligh.

--- After playtest ---
I made all three suggested fixes, and the revised deck was accepted.

1. **No enchantment removal:** I cut 2 Fire // Ice for 2 Hull Breach ({R}{G}: destroy an artifact, an enchantment, or one of each). Now Solitary Confinement, Seal of Cleansing or Aura of Silence no longer shut the deck down in game 1. The 3 Naturalize stay in the sideboard, which gives you 5 answers after sideboarding against Enchantress. I kept it at 2 main deck because more would cost threats or cards that use lands. The checker wanted 6+ copies of anything that supports the engine, so I explained why 2 is enough here.
2. **Too few basics for the rebuy cards:** I cut 3 Karplusan Forest for 2 Mountain and 1 Forest. You now have 13 basics (8 Mountain, 5 Forest) out of 25 lands for Groundskeeper and Harvest Wurm to bring back. Colors still work: the deck check counts 19 red and 16 green sources.
3. **Too many Mox Diamonds:** I cut 1 Mox Diamond for a 4th Call of the Herd. Three Moxes still give a fast turn-2 Seismic Assault, and the Elephant is a sturdier threat that doesn't use up a land you'd rather throw for 2 damage.

The win line hasn't changed: Mox Diamond into a turn-2 Seismic Assault, Terravore growing as lands hit the graveyard, Groundskeeper turning spare mana into repeated 2-damage shots, and Lightning Bolt to finish. Hull Breach now protects that line. The submission says the line ends on turn 5. The tool gave 0.4% for having drawn every card in it by turn 5, but that counts all six named cards at once. You don't need all six to win.

results.prompt: Brew me a mono-green Premodern ramp deck built around Rofellos, Llanowar Emissary.
results.text:
I built a mono-green Rofellos ramp deck and the deck checker accepted it. It's a brew: Rofellos has no recent Premodern tournament results, so there's no proven list to copy.

**The plan:** Play a one-mana creature that taps for mana on turn 1, Rofellos on turn 2, then keep adding Forests. Rofellos makes one green mana per Forest, and Wood Elves or Yavimaya Granger each add a Forest, which also gives Rofellos one more mana. Wirewood Symbiote and Quirion Ranger can untap him so he taps twice in a turn. On turns 3–4 that mana goes into:
- **Deranged Hermit:** four 2/2 Squirrels.
- **Plow Under:** puts two of the opponent's lands back on top of their library.
- **Masticore:** turns spare mana into 1 damage at a time to creatures.

Then Kamahl, Fist of Krosa pumps your whole team +3/+3 with trample for {2}{G}{G}{G}. Any leftover mana pays for more pumps or turns Forests into extra 1/1 attackers. That should win around turn 5.

**The directions I considered:**
1. **Pure Forest ramp:** Wood Elves, Plow Under and big creatures like Verdant Force or Krosan Tusker.
2. **Winter Orb lock:** Winter Orb stops lands from untapping, but Rofellos still counts tapped Forests.
3. **Borrowing the Elves deck's core cards:** Survival of the Fittest, Priest of Titania, Gaea's Cradle, Wirewood Symbiote, Quirion Ranger, Deranged Hermit and Masticore.

**Why I chose direction 3:** I picked the Elves package (option 3) with the basics, Wood Elves and Plow Under from option 1 added in. Elves is a proven Premodern deck (33 recent lists), and Survival of the Fittest finds Rofellos. Rofellos is legendary, so you can't keep two in play, but spare copies are free cards to discard to Survival or to Masticore's upkeep cost. Rofellos is also an Elf, so he adds mana to Priest of Titania.

**Lands and early odds:**
- **Lands:** 15 basic Forests and 3 Gaea's Cradle. Basics make Rofellos stronger; the Elves deck usually adds fetch lands and splash colours, but this one stays mono-green.
- **Turn-2 odds:** You'll have a turn-1 creature that makes mana about 71% of the time. You'll have Rofellos or Survival by turn 2 about 71% of the time. Both together happen about 48% of the time. Survival usually delivers Rofellos a turn later.
- **The checker's 0.1% figure:** It measures how often you'd draw every card in my sample line by turn 5. That figure is misleading, because the line has interchangeable parts: any of 10 early mana creatures, Survival to fetch the key pieces, and Hermit or Masticore as other payoffs.

**Sideboard:** It targets the decks that are doing well right now:
- **Graveyard decks (Replenish, Psychatog):** Naturalize, Tranquil Domain and Tormod's Crypt.
- **Burn (Sligh):** Spike Feeder, a second Ravenous Baloth and Wall of Blossoms.
- **Lock-up option:** Winter Orb, which Rofellos ignores.

--- After playtest ---
I fixed all three problems. The deck is still 60 cards and legal, and the main plan is the same: Rofellos ramp into Deranged Hermit and the Kamahl overrun.

1. **No enchantment answers (fixed, with a change to the suggested fix):** I added 2 Tranquility and a 2nd Nantuko Vigilante. Tranquility destroys all enchantments and doesn't target, so it gets around Sterling Grove's shroud. Survival can now find either Vigilante. I put in 2 Tranquility instead of 3 because it also destroys our own Survival of the Fittest and Sylvan Library. The 3rd copy went to the sideboard. To make room I cut the main Ravenous Baloth and 1 Plow Under. I kept Masticore (see point 2).

2. **Every win needed combat (fixed):** I cut 1 Deranged Hermit, so 2 remain, and moved Hurricane from the sideboard to the main deck. Hurricane deals X damage to each player, so the 10+ mana from Rofellos and Gaea's Cradle now wins without attacking. That covers Elephant Grass, fogs and lock pieces. Hurricane also hits us, so cast it when we have the higher life total or when X is lethal. I kept Masticore because it's another mana sink: {2} to ping a creature, {2} to regenerate. Having one fewer Hermit also means less echo eating turn 4.

3. **Wall of Roots was weak (fixed):** I cut both. One slot went to a 16th Forest, which helps Rofellos and the missed land drops. The other went toward the changes above.

The overall swaps: −2 Wall of Roots, −1 Deranged Hermit, −1 Ravenous Baloth, −1 Plow Under. +1 Forest, +2 Tranquility, +1 Nantuko Vigilante, +1 Hurricane. In the sideboard, Hurricane is replaced by the 3rd Tranquility.

The check after submitting said that 0% of games draw every card in the win line by turn 5. That's expected: it counts every card in the line, some of which are single copies, and it doesn't count tutors. In practice Survival finds the missing pieces, and the line only needs Rofellos plus one finisher.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
I built a **highlander (all 1-of) Dimir combo-control deck**. It's a brew, legal in Legacy, with a 60-card main deck and a 15-card sideboard.

**How it wins:** Cast Thassa's Oracle (UU). While its enter-the-battlefield trigger is on the stack, cast Tainted Pact (1B, instant) and turn down every card it shows you. Pact only stops when it exiles two cards with the same name. Every card in this deck has a different name, basic lands included, so Pact exiles your whole library. The Oracle trigger then resolves with 0 cards left, and 2 devotion is at least 0, so you win. That's 4 mana, all at instant speed. Backup: if Laboratory Maniac or Jace, Wielder of Mysteries is on the battlefield, cast Pact at the end of the opponent's turn and your next draw wins.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Singleton Dimir with the Dimir Tempo package as 1-ofs (chosen).** It takes Force of Will, Daze, Brainstorm, Ponder, Thoughtseize, Fatal Push, Flow State and Snuff Out from the menu, plus Dimir Tempo's mana base. Around them sits a tutor package: Muddle the Mixture, Spellseeker, Solve the Equation, Grim Tutor, Diabolic Intent, Insatiable Avarice, Waterlogged Teachings, Intuition and Merchant Scroll.
2. **The Doomsday shell from the menu.** I dropped it because its 4-ofs break Pact: it would stop on the first duplicate and become a weak tutor.
3. **Slower Esper or Grixis highlander control.** It has more removal but less protection on the combo turn.

I chose #1 because Pact only works when the deck is fully singleton, and the menu's tempo cards stay strong as 1-ofs. The one real list that runs both cards is built this way too: a singleton Dimir rogue list.

**What it costs and how fast it is:**
- Oracle and Pact can't be 4-ofs, because a duplicate stops Pact early.
- Drawing both naturally is rare. The checker gives under 1% for having every card in the win line by turn 5, though it doesn't count tutors or card draw.
- By turn 4 you see Pact or a tutor that finds it 83% of the time, and some combo piece or tutor 93% of the time.
- Expect to win around turns 5–7, protected by 8 counterspells and 3 discard spells, while Bowmasters, Kaito and the removal slow the opponent down.
- When the checker flagged Preordain and Insatiable Avarice as rarely played, I gave reasons in my response to keep them. Part of the Avarice reason was garbled: it said "Wishclaw-free slots," but there's no Wishclaw in the deck. The accurate count is that Grim Tutor, Insatiable Avarice and Diabolic Intent are the three tutors that can find any card.

**Important when sideboarding:** No sideboard card shares a name with a main-deck card. Never board in a second copy of anything, or Pact stops short.

--- After playtest ---
I fixed all three problems and the deck was accepted. Every card is still a one-of: Tainted Pact stops as soon as it exiles two cards with the same name, so a second Force of Will, Brainstorm, Island or Swamp would break the main win.

**1. The combo was too slow to put together.** I cut Insatiable Avarice and Jace, Wielder of Mysteries.
- **Demonic Consultation is banned in Legacy**, so I added Doomsday and Personal Tutor instead.
- **Doomsday** (BBB, and Dark Ritual helps) is a full second route to the win. It can pull Thassa's Oracle from the library or graveyard. You stack five cards: Consider, any card, Thassa's Oracle, then two more. Next turn you draw Consider, cast it for U, mill one card and draw the Oracle. Casting the Oracle for UU with 2 cards left in the library wins.
- **Personal Tutor** costs U and finds Doomsday, so a new cheap tutor replaces the 5-mana one.

**2. Force of Will had too little to pitch, and the deck split between tempo and combo.** I cut Kaito and Toxic Deluge (Deluge moved to the sideboard in place of Hurkyl's Recall).
- **Misdirection** is a free blue spell that Force of Will can also pitch.
- **Pact of Negation** is a free counter for the turn you go off. Its upkeep cost doesn't matter if you've already won.
- Personal Tutor is blue as well, so the deck now has three more blue cards and two more free counters to protect the combo turn.

results.text:
I built you a Glimpse Elves brew for Legacy. It passed the deck check with no errors or warnings.

**The plan:** Play one-mana Elves on turns 1–2. Then, around turn 3–4, cast Glimpse of Nature so every creature you cast that turn draws a card. Heritage Druid taps three Elves for GGG, even ones that just came into play. Nettle Sentinel untaps every time you cast a green spell, so the Sentinels can be tapped for Druid again and again. Wirewood Symbiote returns an Elf to your hand to untap the Druid or Gaea's Cradle, and you recast that Elf for another draw. Once the board is wide, Natural Order (sacrificing a used-up Elf) or Green Sun's Zenith for X=8 puts Craterhoof Behemoth into play. It gives your creatures haste, trample and +X/+X, which should be lethal that turn.

**The directions I considered:**
1. **Classic mono-green Glimpse Elves:** pure combo, Priest of Titania, almost no interaction.
2. **Golgari Elves:** built around Grist and main-deck Thoughtseize; more disruption, but a weaker combo turn.
3. **The Elves version of GX Midrange, with the Glimpse engine added (chosen):** this is the green deck that's actually putting up results right now.

I chose option 3 because it combines the proven parts of current green decks with the engine you asked for:
- **From GX Midrange:** Quirion Ranger, Wirewood Symbiote, Badgermole Cub, Formidable Speaker, Eladamri, Green Sun's Zenith, Once Upon a Time, Natural Order into Craterhoof, Gaea's Cradle, and the Bayou/fetchland mana. Those cards show up together in 56 recent GX lists.
- **What I added:** Glimpse, Heritage Druid and Nettle Sentinel.
- **Allosaurus Shepherd:** another one-drop Elf for the Druid to tap, and it makes your green spells (Glimpse included) impossible to counter. That matters against the Force of Will and Daze decks at the top of the format.

**Caveats:**
- **No list exists yet:** no published list in the last 400 days runs Glimpse and Heritage Druid together, so this is untested.
- **The latest GX list is a different deck:** its newest top finish is a Wight of the Reliquary/Moonshadow build with no Elves engine, so I built from the Elves version of GX instead.
- **Odds by turn 4 (on the play, before mulligans):**
  - You have Glimpse 52.8% of the time.
  - You can reach Heritage Druid 83.1% of the time, counting Green Sun's Zenith for X=1 and Once Upon a Time.
  - You can reach a way to put out Craterhoof (Natural Order or Green Sun's Zenith) 74.1% of the time.
  - All three together: 29.9%.
- **Glimpse isn't required:** the deck can still win with Cradle and Druid mana into Natural Order without it.
- **Only 18 lands:** real GX lists run about 21. The average card costs 1.64 and 30 cards cost one mana, but you may want a 19th land if you're stumbling.
- **Badgermole Cub doesn't boost Heritage Druid, and only works on creatures:** the Cub adds G when you tap a creature for mana. Druid's cost taps other Elves instead of itself, so I'm assuming it doesn't count. Cradle is a land, so it doesn't count either. The Cub pays off with Fyndhorn and Llanowar Elves.

**Sideboard:** Force of Vigor, Endurance, Leyline of the Void, Thoughtseize, Abrupt Decay, Snuff Out and Collector Ouphe. They're aimed at the graveyard, artifact and combo decks in the current field, and at Dimir Tempo.

--- After playtest ---
I made all three fixes. The deck is still 60 cards and legal, and it wins the same way: chain Elves under Glimpse of Nature, then use Natural Order or Green Sun's Zenith to get Craterhoof Behemoth.

1. **Too few mana Elves: fixed as suggested.** I cut 2 Badgermole Cub and added 2 Elvish Mystic. You're right that Cub isn't an Elf. Elvish Mystic is an Elf that taps for G for one mana, so the deck now has 5 Elves that make G for one mana, and Heritage Druid has more bodies to tap. Losing one dork to Bowmasters shouldn't stall the engine as often now.

2. **Too many non-creature spells: fixed as suggested.** I cut 1 Natural Order and added a second Elvish Visionary. Visionary is a two-mana Elf that draws a card when it enters, so it keeps the chain going with or without Glimpse. Natural Order drops to 2 copies because it only has one real target. Green Sun's Zenith still finds Craterhoof as a backup.

3. **Too many lands: mostly fixed.** I cut one Bayou, not both, and added Birchlore Rangers. Birchlore can tap two Elves for mana of any color, and it's another one-drop for Glimpse. You're right that Bayou does nothing in the main deck. But the sideboard has 7 black cards (Thoughtseize, Abrupt Decay and Snuff Out), so I kept one Bayou for after sideboarding. The fetch lands can still find it.

The deck now runs 17 lands, 33 one-drops, an average mana value of 1.53, and 16 Elves Heritage Druid can tap. It still plans to win on turn 4. The draw check says you'll almost never draw every card in the win line naturally by turn 4. That check doesn't count tutors or card draw, so the deck relies on Green Sun's Zenith, Natural Order, Glimpse and Visionary to find the pieces.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Auriok Salvagers and Lion's Eye Diamond.
results.text:
I built a **Salvagers Stompy** brew for Legacy, adapted from the Mono-White Stompy decks that already run these two cards.

**How it wins:** Auriok Salvagers' ability ({1}{W}: return an artifact with mana value 1 or less from your graveyard to your hand) doesn't require tapping, so it works the turn Salvagers comes down. Each loop goes like this:
1. Cast Lion's Eye Diamond for free and sacrifice it for WWW.
2. Pay {1}{W} to return it to your hand and cast it again.

Each loop gains you one white mana, so you can make as much as you want. Lion's Eye Diamond discards your hand, but that doesn't hurt you here. Walking Ballista has mana value 0 in the graveyard, so Salvagers can return it too. You then cast it with a huge X and shoot the opponent out. Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors and Lotus Petal can get the 4-mana Salvagers down on turn 2 or 3.

**Backups:**
- Karn, the Great Creator can take the sideboard Lion's Eye Diamond or Pyrite Spellbomb into your hand. The sideboard Diamond is there for that.
- Urza's Saga's third chapter puts a Lion's Eye Diamond straight onto the battlefield.
- If Salvagers ends up in the graveyard (discarded or killed), Agatha's Soul Cauldron can exile it. Then any creature of yours with a +1/+1 counter gets the Salvagers ability. Leonardo, The Destined White Mage and Ballista all get counters.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. A blue cantrip shell borrowing Brainstorm, Ponder and Force of Will from Dimir Tempo. It's too slow to cast a 4-drop combo creature.
2. A graveyard version built around the Cauldron package that Sewer Combo uses. It's too dependent on getting Salvagers into the graveyard first.
3. A mono-white shell with fast mana, Chalice of the Void and Karn (my pick). It's the strongest because the fast mana makes Salvagers castable early, and Karn and Urza's Saga double as tutors for the missing piece.

**Honest odds** (no mulligans, seeing 9 cards by turn 3 on the play):
- Salvagers itself: about 49%.
- Some way to get a Diamond (one of the 3 Diamonds, 4 Karns or 4 Sagas): about 86%.
- Both together: about 41%.

When the combo doesn't come together, Chalice and Ethersworn Canonist slow the opponent down while the creatures attack. Treat it as a turn 3–4 combo deck, not a turn-2 one.

--- After playtest ---
I made all three suggested fixes. The new list was accepted.

**1. Mana base: fixed.** I cut 3 City of Traitors and 1 Urza's Saga for 2 Plains and 2 Mox Diamond, plus a third extra Plains (explained under 3). That's 19 lands: 9 Plains, Karakas, 4 Ancient Tomb, 3 Saga and 2 Cavern. The deck checker counts 24 white sources. Mox Diamond costs 0 and makes any color, so a Wasteland on Ancient Tomb no longer leaves you stuck on one Cavern.

**2. The combo was diluted: fixed.** I cut 4 Leonardo and 3 The Destined White Mage. In their place:
- the 4th Lion's Eye Diamond
- a 4th Walking Ballista
- 4 Enlightened Tutor, which costs W and puts an artifact (LED or Ballista) on top of your library

Between the 4 Tutors and the 3 Urza's Sagas, you now have 7 ways to find a missing piece. I kept Haliya because it gains 1 life whenever an artifact enters, so it gains life on every LED recast.

**3. Agatha's Soul Cauldron: fixed.** I cut both Cauldrons for a second Mox Opal and a third Ethersworn Canonist. Canonist limits each player to one nonartifact spell per turn. That shuts off cantrip chains, but your artifact combo still works.

**Count and sideboard changes:**
- The changes left the main deck at 59 cards, so I added a 9th Plains to make 60.
- Since there are now 4 LEDs in the main deck, the sideboard LED had to go. I replaced it with Mycosynth Lattice for Karn to fetch.
- The sideboard's second Ethersworn Canonist would have made 5 total, so I swapped it for Defense Grid. Defense Grid makes each spell cost {3} more except on its controller's turn, which helps you combo through countermagic.

**Odds:** The submission tool calculated a 0.3% chance of drawing every card in the win line by turn 3. That number is misleading. The tool required all six listed cards, including backups like Karn and the Tutor, and it doesn't account for tutors. The real combo is Auriok Salvagers + LED + Ballista plus 4 mana, and Tutor or Saga can supply the missing piece. I didn't calculate the actual odds of assembling that by turn 3.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Hypergenesis.
results.text:
This is a brew: **Temur Hypergenesis Cascade**, a Legacy deck that cheats fatties into play on turn 2 or 3. It's legal and was accepted.

**The plan:** Cast Violent Outburst or Shardless Agent (both cost 3) on turn 3, or on turn 2 by exiling Elvish Spirit Guide for extra mana. Cascade casts the first card it finds that costs less than 3 mana and isn't a land. Hypergenesis is the only such card in the deck, so it's cast for free every time. Then you dump your hand onto the battlefield:
- **Archon of Cruelty:** the opponent sacrifices a creature, discards a card and loses 3 life.
- **Fury:** comes in without being sacrificed and splits 4 damage among whatever creatures the opponent put down.
- **Atraxa:** refills your hand.
- **Emrakul:** a 15/15 that ends the game in one or two attacks.

Violent Outburst is an instant, so you can cascade at the end of the opponent's turn and attack first. Four Force of Will and two Force of Negation protect the combo.

**Why this direction:** I compared three:
1. Temur, using the Living End deck's cascade setup (played in 11 recent lists).
2. Bant (green-white-blue) with Ardent Plea and Solitude.
3. Grixis (blue-black-red) with Demonic Dread.

Temur won because it gets both of the best 3-mana cascade spells, and the Living End setup is proven: free counters, Spirit Guides, and mana from real lists. The one big change: Living End's small cycling creatures became fatties, plus cyclers (Striped Riverwinder, Street Wraith, Curator) that you can either cycle to dig for the combo or drop into play as bodies.

**Things to know:**
- **Card costs matter.** The only card in the deck costing less than 3 is Hypergenesis, so the cascade can't miss. Elvish Spirit Guide technically costs 3, so the cascade skips it too. That's why there's no Bloodbraid Elf (it costs 4, so its cascade could hit the 3-cost cards) and no cheap blue counters like Hydroblast.
- **3 Hypergenesis, not 4.** You only need one left in your library, and copies you draw are slow (you'd have to wait three turns).
- **15 lands, despite the checker's warning to run 22.** Real Living End lists average 14.55. Here the cyclers and Generous Ent help find lands, and the expensive cards are never cast normally.
- **Zero black sources is on purpose.** Griselbrand and Archon only ever come in through Hypergenesis.
- **The checker's 0.1% for the win line is misleading.** That's the chance of drawing every card I listed by turn 4. You really only need one cascade spell plus two or three big cards in hand.
- **Odds:** about 75% to have a cascade spell by turn 3, before counting the cycling. About 26% to cascade on turn 2 with a Spirit Guide.
- **The risks:** Hypergenesis also lets the opponent put permanents from their hand into play, and Chalice of the Void set to 0 counters the free Hypergenesis. The sideboard's Force of Vigor is there for Chalice, and the Fury and Archon triggers help clean up whatever the opponent drops.

--- After playtest ---
I resubmitted the deck and it was accepted. I made two of the three suggested fixes and rejected the Pyroblast swap.

1. **Too slow and mana-fragile: fixed as suggested.** I cut 2 Curator of Mysteries for 2 Simian Spirit Guide. The deck now has 6 Spirit Guides, so turn-2 Violent Outburst no longer depends on one third land surviving Wasteland, and Fury gets more red cards to pitch. Simian Spirit Guide has mana value 3, so the cascade still always hits Hypergenesis.

2. **Force of Negation dead on my turn: kept it and turned down Pyroblast.** Pyroblast has mana value 1, so every Violent Outburst or Shardless Agent cascade could hit it instead of Hypergenesis. That would break the deck. I looked for another counterspell that is free on my own turn and costs at least 3, and found nothing; Force of Will remains the only one. The extra Spirit Guides make it easier to cast Outburst at the end of the opponent's turn, which is the line the deck should aim for. That is also when Force of Negation is free.

3. **Hedge Maze: fixed as suggested.** I swapped it for a basic Mountain. All lands now enter untapped, and Scalding Tarn can fetch red through Wasteland.

The sideboard is unchanged. Everything in it costs 3 or more, so none of it can be hit by cascade.

Things to know about the submitted list:
- **Land count:** The checker flagged 15 lands as low; similar decks usually run about 22. I kept 15 on purpose. The plan is to cascade on turns 2–3 with Spirit Guide help, and Hypergenesis puts extra lands and creatures from hand onto the battlefield anyway.
- **Griselbrand:** It has no black sources and can't be cast normally. It only ever enters through Hypergenesis.
- **The 0% odds:** The tool reported 0% for drawing every card in the win line by turn 2. It counts the full sample line (Archon of Cruelty, Fury, Atraxa and Emrakul together), but the deck only needs a cascade card, mana for it, and any few big creatures in hand.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Scapeshift and Valakut, the Molten Pinnacle.
results.text:
I built **RG Valakut Ramp** for Legacy, labelled a brew. Nobody has played Scapeshift and Valakut in Legacy in the last 90 days: Scapeshift appears in one Rogue list and Valakut in none. All 82 real decks running the pair are Modern decks (Amulet Titan and RG Valakut).

**The plan:** Play a mana creature on turn 1, then ramp with Sakura-Tribe Elder and Dryad of the Ilysian Grove. Once you have 7 lands, cast Scapeshift: sacrifice them all and fetch Valakut plus 6 Mountains. They all enter at once, so Valakut triggers 6 times for 18 damage, or 21 with 8 lands. In Legacy, Taiga and Stomping Ground are Mountains, so they count. While Dryad is out, every land you control is a Mountain.

**Backup plans:**
- Primeval Titan fetches Valakut and Mountains when it enters and each time it attacks. Green Sun's Zenith can find it, Dryad, a mana creature or Elder.
- Crop Rotation sacrifices a land at instant speed to put Valakut into play. Once Valakut is out, it can fetch a Mountain for one more 3-damage trigger.
- Lightning Bolt and Veil of Summer protect the combo against the blue tempo decks.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. A Lands-style shell: Exploration, Mox Diamond, Crop Rotation, Life from the Loam.
2. A Temur list with Brainstorm, Ponder and Force of Will. The dual lands double as Mountains.
3. A green ramp shell taken from GX Midrange: Green Sun's Zenith, mana creatures, Once Upon a Time.

I went with the third, keeping Crop Rotation from the Lands package. It gets to 7 lands and 4 mana fastest, and Green Sun's Zenith gives the Titan backup more ways to show up.

**Odds:** You'll see Scapeshift, Titan or Zenith by turn 5 in about 91% of games (no mulligans). You'll have both one of those and an early ramp card in about 85%. The target is a turn-5 kill. The checker's 0.1% figure for that turn assumes you draw every card in the line. The deck doesn't need all of them, so that number understates it.

**Mana:** The deck has 18 green sources against about 21 in real GX lists. I did that on purpose to keep 12 Mountains in the library for Scapeshift and Titan to fetch.

**Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks:
- Pyroblast and Choke for Dimir and Izzet Tempo.
- Fury for Ocelot and Eldrazi.
- Force of Vigor, Endurance, Grafdigger's Cage and Damping Sphere for Tron, Reanimator, Sewer Combo and Storm.

--- After playtest ---
I took all three fixes. The resubmitted deck passed the legality check and was accepted.

**Changes:** cut 3 Crop Rotation, 2 Sylvan Library and 1 Forest. Added 1 Lightning Bolt, 2 Fiery Confluence, 2 Veil of Summer and 1 Valakut, the Molten Pinnacle.

1. **Cheap interaction (fixed):** Bolt goes up to 4, and I added 2 Fiery Confluence. Choosing its "1 damage to each creature" mode once kills Bowmasters, Army tokens and a flipped Delver. The other two modes can be 2 damage to the opponent each, which adds reach on top of Valakut. The catch is that the 1-damage sweep also kills my own Hierarchs, Elves and Tribe Elders, so it's best cast once those have already done their job. It's also a 4-mana sorcery, so it's a catch-up card, not a turn-1 answer.
2. **Too slow and easy to counter (fixed):** I cut Sylvan Library for 2 more Veil of Summer, so the deck runs the maximum 4. Veil stops Force of Will and Daze from countering Scapeshift or Titan on the key turn, and draws a card when the opponent cast a blue or black spell that turn. The submit tool flagged 4 protection cards as below its usual floor of 6. I kept 4 because it's the maximum allowed, the 3 sideboard Pyroblasts come in against blue decks, and spare mana from the dorks helps beat Daze.
3. **Crop Rotation (fixed):** All 3 are gone, since the card cost a land in a deck that needs lots of lands. A 3rd Valakut takes the Forest's slot, so one Wasteland or a bad draw no longer strands Scapeshift. Taiga, Stomping Ground and basic Mountains still give 12 Mountains to fetch. The deck has 21 red sources and 17 green.

The deck's plan is the same: ramp with dorks and Sakura-Tribe Elder, protect the key turn with Veil, then Scapeshift into Valakut plus 6 Mountains for 18 damage. Primeval Titan is the backup. The tool reported 0% for drawing every card in the win line by turn 5. That's expected, because the line lists alternatives like Dryad and Titan that you never need all at once, and the tool doesn't count tutors like Green Sun's Zenith.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker and Pestermite.
results.text:
I built a Legacy deck where Kiki-Jiki and Pestermite combine for an infinite combo, which I'm calling **Izzet Kiki Twin**. No published list in the last 400 days plays these two cards together, so this is a brew.

**How it wins:** Get Pestermite onto the battlefield, often by flashing it in at the end of the opponent's turn. Then Kiki-Jiki, which has haste, taps to make a hasty token copy of Pestermite. The copy's enter ability untaps Kiki. Repeat as many times as you like, then attack with that many 2/1 flyers. The deck plans to do this on turn 5.

**Backup pieces:**
- **Deceiver Exarch (4):** works like a second set of Pestermites, since it can also untap Kiki.
- **Splinter Twin (3):** a 4-mana stand-in for Kiki. Put it on Pestermite or Exarch and the loop works the same way.
- **Imperial Recruiter (4):** can fetch Kiki itself (power 2) or whichever missing creature you need.

Counting all of these, you have at least one copy card and one untap creature in about 73% of games by turn 5, before counting your card-selection spells. If you only count the two named cards, both are in hand by turn 5 in just 26% of games, mulligans included. That's why the backup copies are there.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Izzet tempo with the combo added (chosen).** It borrows the Izzet Tempo package (Brainstorm, Ponder, 4 Force of Will, 4 Lightning Bolt) to protect the combo and keep you alive.
2. **Jeskai midrange.** This adds Restoration Angel and Village Bell-Ringer as extra loop pieces with Kiki. I passed because white makes Kiki's three red mana even harder to pay for.
3. **Sneak Attack shell.** I passed because Kiki already has haste, so Sneak Attack adds little.

I chose the Izzet version because it has the most ways to finish the combo, the strongest protection, and the cleanest red mana.

**Changes from Izzet Tempo:**
- **20 lands, not the usual 19.** These include 16 red sources, about double the usual Izzet Tempo count, so you can pay for Kiki.
- **No Wasteland or Daze.** Daze returns one of your lands to your hand, which slows you down when you need five lands for Kiki.
- **Kiki at 3 copies.** It's legendary and costs 5, so extra copies would get stuck in your hand. Recruiter and Twin cover the gap.
- **2 Force of Negation instead of Counterspell.** The deck checker flagged Counterspell as almost never played in Legacy, so I swapped it out.

The sideboard is aimed at the current top decks:
- **Blood Moon:** against Tron, Lands and Eldrazi.
- **Pyroblast and Hydroblast:** for blue and red decks.
- **Consign to Memory, Surgical Extraction and Grafdigger's Cage:** against graveyard and combo decks.

--- After playtest ---
I took all three fixes. On the first one I made a different cut than you suggested.

1. **Combo too slow:** I took out all 4 Imperial Recruiter for 4 Daze but kept all 3 Kiki-Jiki instead of cutting one. Recruiter was the slow part, not Kiki. Kiki is the card you asked for, and it's the backup copy engine that still works when the opponent has an answer to Splinter Twin. The deck now plays as Twin-tempo: flash in Pestermite or Deceiver Exarch at the opponent's end step, put Splinter Twin on it on turn 4, and protect that turn with 10 counterspells (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation). Kiki on turn 5 is the plan B.
2. **Too few answers:** I cut Preordain and Spell Pierce for a 2nd Brazen Borrower and a 2nd Fire // Ice. Fire can kill two small creatures at once (like Bowmasters and its tokens), Ice can tap a blocker or a land and draws a card, and Borrower can bounce Murktide Regent or a blocker. That's 8 answers to creatures now instead of 6. Dropping a cantrip also means Bowmasters punishes you a little less.
3. **Tapped land:** Thundering Falls is now a 3rd basic Island. Your fetch lands always find an untapped land that Wasteland can't hit, and Daze has more Islands to return.

With 6 copy engines, 8 untap creatures and 8 cantrips, the turn-4 kill takes some luck. The deck checker gives a 21% chance of having drawn the whole combo by turn 4, but that number ignores Brainstorm and Ponder digging for pieces, so your real odds are better. The sideboard is the same. The deck is legal at exactly 60 cards with 20 lands.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Wildfire.
results.text:
I built a mono-red artifact-ramp Wildfire deck (a brew; the tool found no published list running Wildfire in the last 400 days). The plan is to sweep the opponent's lands with Wildfire, then win with Magnivore. You play Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors, Mind Stone, Fire Diamond and Thran Dynamo, which lets you cast Wildfire around turn 4–5. Each player sacrifices four lands and every creature takes 4 damage, but your rocks aren't lands, so you keep your mana while the opponent loses most of theirs. Next comes Magnivore (haste). Its power and toughness equal the number of sorceries in all graveyards, and every Wildfire, Stone Rain, Pillage, Firebolt and Pyroclasm counts, so it usually lands as a 4/4 to 8/8. Masticore can regenerate through the sweep, and Rorix Bladewing is a 6/5 flier with haste that survives 4 damage. Early on, Stone Rain, Pillage, Lightning Bolt, Firebolt and Pyroclasm keep you alive and hold the opponent's mana down.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-red artifact ramp:** fast mana borrowed from Welder Prison, the land destruction suite from Mono-Red Land Destruction, plus Magnivore.
2. **Red-green Terravore:** the Terrageddon package of Mox Diamond, Terravore and Sylvan Library. Every Wildfire puts eight lands in graveyards, which grows Terravore.
3. **Blue-red Welder Prison:** Goblin Welder, Tangle Wire and Tinker with Wildfire added.

I picked the first because Wildfire is strongest when most of your mana isn't lands, and staying mono-red keeps the double-red costs reliable. It also lets Magnivore count every sorcery in the deck.

**Notes:**
- **Land count:** The checker flagged 21 lands against about 26 in Mono-Red Land Destruction lists. I kept 21 because the 11 mana rocks bring the deck to 32 mana sources. If you play a land early and give up City of Traitors, that's usually fine.
- **Odds:** The tool rated the full winning sequence at 0.4% by turn 6. That number requires drawing all seven named cards. Realistically you need Wildfire, enough mana and a threat. With only 4 Wildfires, many games will be won by Stone Rain, burn and Magnivore without it.
- **Sideboard:** Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast are for Stiflenought and Psychatog, and Anarchy is for Enchantress. Tormod's Crypt is for Hermit Druid and Replenish, Earthquake for Sligh and Goblins, and Overload for Mox Diamond and other artifacts.

--- After playtest ---
I changed seven cards in the main deck and left the sideboard as it was.

1. **Too much mana: fixed.** I cut 2 Mountain and Rorix Bladewing. I couldn't add Grim Monolith because it's banned in Premodern. Instead I added card flow and threats:
   - **2 Lay Waste:** a land-destruction sorcery that can cycle away for a new card when you're flooded.
   - **1 Cursed Scroll:** a cheap artifact, so Wildfire doesn't destroy it. It keeps doing damage once Wildfire has emptied both players' hands.

   The deck now has 19 lands plus 11 rocks (was 21 lands). The deck checker recommends about 23 lands, but the rocks make up the difference.

2. **Lightning Bolt: fixed.** I swapped the 4 Bolts for 2 Rolling Thunder, 1 Fireball and a 4th Pillage. All of these are sorceries, so each one makes Magnivore bigger once it's in a graveyard. The X spells also use the leftover rock mana after Wildfire, either to clear blockers or to finish the opponent. Almost every nonland card except the creatures and artifacts is now a sorcery.

3. **No way to remove enchantments: kept as it was.** The sideboard already has 3 Anarchy. Against Enchantress, bring them in and take out Pyroclasm. I didn't put Anarchy in the main deck, because in other matchups it's a dead card and the deck needs to work against the whole field.

The plan is the same: rocks into a turn 4–5 Wildfire, then a big hasty Magnivore. Firebolt, Rolling Thunder and Fireball help finish the game.

To be honest about the odds: you'll draw every card in the full win line by turn 6 in only about 0.6% of games. That's because the line names seven specific cards. Each step has backups (other rocks for Mind Stone, Pillage and Lay Waste for Stone Rain, Fireball for Rolling Thunder), so in practice the game plan comes together much more often than that number suggests.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Zur's Weirding.
results.text:
I built **UW Weirding Control**, a brew that plays 4 Zur's Weirding on top of the borrowed UW Standstill control shell, and the deck was accepted.

**The plan:** Zur's Weirding reveals both hands. Every time your opponent would draw, you can pay 2 life to send that card to the graveyard instead. With the lock up, they're stuck with only the cards already in their hand, and you can see them. You handle those with 4 Counterspell, 2 Mana Leak, 3 Absorb, 4 Swords to Plowshares and 2 Wrath of God.

The lock costs life, so the deck is built to make life:
- **Words of Worship** turns your own draw into 5 life for {1}. That pays for two denied opponent draws a turn, and it also stops them from denying your draw.
- **Exalted Angel** gains 4 life every time it hits while it beats down.
- **Absorb** gains 3 life while countering.

**Your own cards still flow.** Impulse and Fact or Fiction don't use the word "draw," so the opponent can't use Weirding to deny them. Enlightened Tutor finds Weirding. You see Weirding or a Tutor by turn 4 in about 68% of games.

**The win:** lock up around turn 4, then win with Angel, Decree of Justice tokens or Mishra's Factory, usually around turn 8.

**Honest odds:** the checker says you'll have drawn every card in the full win line by turn 8 in only 1.6% of games. That number is misleading: it doesn't count Enlightened Tutor or Impulse digging, and the line doesn't need every piece. The real core is Weirding plus any one life source plus your counters, and the rest is interchangeable.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **UW control with the Standstill package (chosen).**
2. **Bant Parfait:** Oath of Druids, Gush, Accumulated Knowledge and Gaea's Blessing. The only real decks with Weirding are built this way, but they play it as a single toolbox card.
3. **Prison:** Weirding with Armageddon or Sphere of Resistance.

I picked the Standstill shell because it already plays a game about denying cards and already runs Exalted Angel, which pays for Weirding.

**Card note:** the checker flagged Absorb, which shows up in only about 1% of recent decks; players usually choose Foil or Daze at that cost. I kept it because its 3 life directly pays for denied draws, and Foil and Daze gain nothing.

The sideboard is aimed at the current meta:
- **Sligh:** 2 Circle of Protection: Red and 2 Blue Elemental Blast.
- **Combo and Enchantress:** 3 Meddling Mage.
- **Graveyard decks:** 2 Tormod's Crypt.
- **Terrageddon's land destruction:** 2 Teferi's Response.

--- After playtest ---
I resubmitted the deck with four card swaps. The plan is the same: land Zur's Weirding and win with Exalted Angel.

**1. Enchantment answers (fixed):** I cut 1 Swords to Plowshares and 1 Mana Leak, and added a second Disenchant and 1 Seal of Cleansing to the main deck. These cards earn their spot beyond the Enchantress matchup: they also clear hate enchantments aimed at Weirding. Enlightened Tutor can fetch Seal of Cleansing, since it's an enchantment. The deck now runs 3 main-deck answers to artifacts and enchantments, plus 2 more in the sideboard.

**2. Words of Worship (partly fixed):** I cut one copy and added a 4th Exalted Angel. I kept one copy on purpose. Weirding works both ways: "any other player may pay 2 life" to throw away a drawn card, so the opponent can also deny your draws. Words of Worship turns your draw into 5 life instead, which they can't deny. With only one copy you'll rarely draw it with nothing to do, and Tutor can fetch it once the lock is down.

**3. Enlightened Tutor (kept, 2 copies):** Cutting Tutor would make the namesake card show up less often, which is the opposite of the goal. The real problem in the test game was Seal of Cleansing sitting on their side, and the new enchantment removal deals with that. Tutor can also find that removal now.

**Notes:**
- I didn't add another Fact or Fiction. The deck already has 6 ways to dig without drawing (4 Impulse, 2 Fact or Fiction), and both work under the lock.
- The sideboard is unchanged.
- The check tool says the deck has 25 lands, 14 white sources and 16 blue sources.
- The submit tool estimated that you'll have drawn every card in the win line by turn 9 in only about 2% of games. That number is low because the line names six specific cards, and the tool doesn't count Tutor or digging, so it isn't the real chance of winning.

Puts Zur's Weirding on top (or Seal of Cleansing/Words of Worship when needed) so Weirding lands turn 4 more often.
Hands are played revealed; each time the opponent would draw, you may pay 2 life to send that card to the graveyard, leaving them only the cards you can see.
Digs without drawing, so the opponent can't deny it under Weirding; Fact or Fiction works the same way.
Each time it deals damage you gain that much life (4 per swing), which pays for the Weirding denials while it kills in about 5 swings.
Counters the opponent's last real answer from their revealed hand and gains 3 life for the lock.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Squandered Resources and Natural Balance.
results.text:
The deck was accepted as a brew, a Golgari "Squandered Terravore" list. No published list in the last 400 days runs these two cards together.

**How the two cards work together.** Squandered Resources lets you sacrifice a land for one mana, with no other cost. Natural Balance lets a player with four or fewer lands fetch basics until they have five. So the main turn goes like this:
- Tap all your lands, then sacrifice them to Squandered Resources. With 4 lands that's 8 mana.
- Spend 4 of it on Natural Balance with zero lands left, and fetch 5 untapped basics.
- You end the turn with more lands than you started with, plus 4 floating mana and 5 fresh lands to tap.
- Every land you sacrificed goes to the graveyard, and Terravore gets +1/+1 for each land card in all graveyards.

**The plan.** Turn 1 Mox Diamond, discarding a land for an early mana. Turn 2 Squandered Resources. Turn 3 Terravore. On turn 4, do the Natural Balance turn above and spend the leftover mana on a hardcast Krosan Tusker or a big Pernicious Deed. Then win with a 6/6-or-bigger trampling Terravore plus Treetop Village around turns 5–6.

**Directions I considered:**
- **Terravore Rock (chosen):** the Terravore and Mox Diamond package from Terrageddon, on top of Rock's interaction and mana: Deed, Duress, Smother, Llanowar Wastes, 23 lands.
- **Black aggro with Nantuko Shade:** borrowed from Moneyball Black. Sacrificing Swamps would pump Shade, but it's a one-shot win that dies to a single removal spell.
- **Jund burn finish:** use the same big mana turn for a huge X burn spell. Running three colors makes it hard to keep enough basics for Natural Balance to fetch.

I chose Terravore Rock because Terravore is the one payoff that turns the lands you sacrifice into a permanent threat.

**Things to know:**
- **The full line rarely comes together.** You'll have both Squandered Resources and Natural Balance by turn 5 only about 31% of the time. Each card still works on its own: Squandered speeds out Terravore and Deed, and Natural Balance alone is ramp.
- **Natural Balance helps your opponent too.** If they have four or fewer lands, they also fetch basics. Cast it when they have five lands, or when your Terravore swing is worth the trade. Against control decks with six or more lands, it destroys their extras.
- **The deck runs 12 basics on purpose.** Natural Balance can only fetch basic lands, so keep that count if you change the mana.

**Sideboard:** Cabal Therapy for the blue decks, Engineered Plague for Goblins and Elves, Naturalize for Enchantress, and Zuran Orb, which also sacrifices lands, for Sligh.

--- After playtest ---
The revised deck is in, with 60 cards. I took the fixes for problems 2 and 3 as suggested. For problem 1, I added the 2 Wasteland but kept all 4 Natural Balance.

**1. Engine with no payoff: partly fixed.** Natural Balance stays at 4 because you asked for a deck built around it. It also already has payoffs. Terravore grows by every land the combo sacrifices. The 8-mana Balance turn then casts Krosan Tusker, Spiritmonger or a big Pernicious Deed in the same turn. Balance also makes an opponent with 6 or more lands sacrifice down to 5.
- I did add **2 Wasteland**, replacing Dust Bowl and one Treetop Village.
- Wasteland destroys Serra's Sanctum and other utility lands. It also puts more lands in the graveyard for Terravore, and Squandered Resources can sacrifice it for mana.
- I didn't cut basics for it, because Balance can only fetch basic lands.

**2. Removal too narrow: fixed as suggested.** I cut Diabolic Edict and 1 Smother for the **4th Pernicious Deed** and **1 Creeping Mold**. Creeping Mold destroys an artifact, enchantment or land. When it hits a land, that's another card in the graveyard for Terravore.

**3. Threats too thin: fixed as suggested.** **2 Spiritmonger** replace 2 Ravenous Baloth. It's a 6/6 that costs 5, so it survives Deed at X of 4 or less. Its {B} regenerate ability also saves it from a bigger Deed, since Deed destroys rather than exiles. It's also a good use for the floating mana after the Balance turn.

The deck passes the legality check with 23 lands. The full win line (Mox Diamond, Squandered Resources, Terravore, Balance, a big threat, Wasteland) only comes together by turn 6 in about 0.6% of games, because it needs six specific cards. The real core is Squandered Resources plus Terravore, and Balance or the big threats close the game.

winLine.does: Turn 1: discard a land to it for an extra mana source. That land is the first one in the graveyard for Terravore.
Turn 2: sacrifice any land to add one mana of a type that land could make.
Turn 3: a trampler whose power and toughness equal the number of land cards in all graveyards. Wasteland, Creeping Mold and fetchlands all add to that count.

Turn 4: tap your 4 lands, then sacrifice them to Squandered for 8 mana. Cast Balance with 4 of it while you control zero lands and fetch 5 basics. Terravore gets at least 4 bigger, and an opponent with 6 or more lands sacrifices down to 5.
Same turn: the 4 floating mana plus the new basics cast a 6/6 that regenerates, or Krosan Tusker, or pay for a big Pernicious Deed.
Turns 5-6: destroy Serra's Sanctum or another utility land. It adds one more land to the graveyard while the two fatties attack.

T3 (draw Smother): Forest, Pernicious Deed. Smother can't touch the shrouded Enchantress. Opp: Enchantress's Presence, Elephant Grass, chains draws. Seal stays home because Deed can respond.

problems.problem: The deck's namesake engine has no payoff. Squandered Resources plus Natural Balance just turns lands into mana and resets to five basics, but nothing in the list converts that into a win except Terravore. Balance is symmetric, so it ramps a mana-light opponent and spares a Serra's Sanctum or Treetop-style land. In this game both cards sat in hand doing nothing while Enchantress built its lock.

problems.fix: Cut Diabolic Edict and 1 Smother for the 4th Pernicious Deed and 1 Creeping Mold, so the deck can answer enchantments, artifacts and key lands like Sanctum or Tolarian Academy.

problems.problem: The threat base is too thin and too slow. After Tusker cycled and Wall died to my own Deed, I never presented a clock. Ravenous Baloth and Wall of Blossoms don't pressure combo-control decks. Meanwhile Mox Diamond was stranded without a spare land and then had no mana sink.
problems.fix: Swap 2 Ravenous Baloth for 2 Spiritmonger, a resilient threat that survives Deed at low X and pressures planeswalker-less control decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a mill deck in premodern
results.text:
I built a UW Standstill-Mill brew. No published Premodern list in the last 400 days pairs Millstone with Traumatize, so this is a new deck rather than a copy of an existing one.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Stiflenought-style mono-blue tempo-mill.** Keep that deck's free spells and cantrips, but replace its creatures with Vision Charm and Brain Freeze. Brain Freeze already shows up in about 93% of Stiflenought sideboards.
2. **Frantic Storm.** A Brain Freeze storm combo deck. It already exists, so building it would just hand you an existing list.
3. **Standstill control with mill as the win condition.** I chose this one. Millstone's ability doesn't count as casting a spell, so it never breaks Standstill. That leaves the opponent two bad options: cast into Standstill and give you 3 cards, or sit still and get milled. This deck also has the Swords and Wraths it needs against the big creature decks (Terrageddon, Sligh, Goblins).

**The plan:** I took the Standstill shell's mana and interaction: 25 lands, 14 white and 18 blue sources, Counterspell, Swords, Wrath and Fact or Fiction. Its Decree of Justice and Mishra's Factory win condition is replaced with mill:
- **Repeatable mill:** 4 Millstone (2 cards a turn) and 1 Ambassador Laquatus (3 cards per activation).
- **Bigger chunks:** Traumatize (mills half their library), 2 Vision Charm (4 cards at instant speed), and 2 Brain Freeze to finish with storm copies at the end of a turn.

You stay behind counters and removal, run Millstone at the end of each of their turns, and close with Traumatize, Vision Charm or Brain Freeze. The target is to empty the library around turn 9–10.

**Things to know:**
- **Millstone odds:** you'll have one by turn 4 in only about 53% of games. Impulse and Fact or Fiction help you find it, and the burst mill spells add some backup.
- **The win line:** the checker found that drawing *every* card in my listed line by turn 10 happens 0.4% of the time. You don't need all of them. Any mix of mill sources that adds up to about 45 cards wins. That's still slow, so expect long games.
- **Hermit Druid Combo:** milling that deck helps it, since it wants its own graveyard full. Against it, plan to counter its spells and bring in the 2 Tormod's Crypt from the sideboard.
- **Sideboard:** aimed at the current field. CoP: Red and the Blasts are for Sligh and Goblins, Annul is for Enchantress and Replenish, and Meddling Mage is for combo decks.

--- After playtest ---
I made all three suggested fixes. The resubmitted deck is legal and has 60 cards.

1. **Enchantment answers:** I cut 2 Powder Keg and added 2 Seal of Cleansing. Keg never hit enchantments and could destroy my own Millstones. Seal destroys an artifact or enchantment, so it can take out Opalescence, Solitary Confinement or Sterling Grove. Alongside the Disenchant that's 3 answers in the main deck. That's still a light count against Enchantress, so the rest belongs in the sideboard.
2. **Mill clock:** I cut 2 Brain Freeze, since nothing in the deck raised its storm count, so it was just a 2-mana mill-3. I added a second Traumatize and a Grindstone in their place.
   - The two Traumatizes mill half the remaining library each, for example 30 down to 15, then 15 down to 7.
   - Grindstone is a second engine you can use every turn. It mills 2 for {3} and keeps going while the two milled cards share a color, which happens often against one- or two-color decks.
   - With Vision Charm and Ambassador Laquatus ({3}: mill 3, as often as you can pay), the deck has 6 cards that mill in big chunks instead of 1.
3. **Mana:** I cut 2 Mishra's Factory and added 1 Plains and 1 Coastal Tower. The deck now has 16 white and 19 blue sources, up from 13–14 white. That's more than real Standstill lists run (about 13 white and 16 blue), so Wrath of God and Counterspell no longer compete for sources. Factory was a beatdown card with no job in this deck.

The plan is the same: hold up counters, then Millstone at the end of their turn and keep Standstill on the board. One honest note: the checker says 0% of games draw every card in the win line by turn 10. That's because the line names several one-ofs, like Grindstone and Laquatus. You don't need all of them to win, just steady Millstone activations plus one or two of the big mill cards.

winLine.does: Played turn 2-3. Each turn, {2},{T} mills the opponent 2 cards at instant speed, usually at the end of their turn.
Second repeatable engine. {3},{T} mills 2, and keeps repeating while the two milled cards share a color, which in mono- or two-color decks often means big chunks.
Mill activations are abilities, not spells, so they never break it. The opponent has to cast into it (we draw 3) or let the mill keep running.
Protects the engines and stops threats. Swords and Wrath handle creatures; Seal of Cleansing and Disenchant handle enchantments and artifacts.
Digs for more mill pieces and counters.
Two copies. Each one mills half of what's left (30 -> 15 -> 7), the bulk of the clock.
Spare mana goes into {3}: mill 3, any number of times, at instant speed.
Instant-speed 4-card mill to finish off the last cards after Traumatize.

I hold Keg because at 2 counters it would also kill my own Millstones. Opp: Enchantress's Presence, then Seal of Cleansing, drawing 2 off each. Library about 44. T4 (draw Counterspell, no land, stuck on 3): hold Counterspell. Opp sacs Seal on Millstone A and casts Sterling Grove, which I counter. Mirri's Guile resolves and they draw 2. I mill 0 this turn.
